prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.76
  gal: 0.24
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Scope
- Applies mainly to England due to devolution. Scottish and Welsh proposals may differ.

Fiscal approach and tax
- Reprioritise about £5bn annually by abolishing certain subsidies and departments/functions, cancelling ID cards, and diverting Child Trust Fund money to education.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate only on earnings above £100,000 to fund: abolition of university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; and cutting local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay.
- Independent scrutiny of budgets by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Typical household local tax bill reduced by about £450 under Local Income Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via expanded access to scans/tests, weekend/evening operation, and staffing/training.
- Free eye and dental checks; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- More clinicians; scrap central targets; more local accountability.
- NHS dentistry contract reform and personal dental plans.
- Health MOTs, personal care plans for long‑term conditions, stronger mental health rights, end age discrimination.
- Public health: school nutrition standards, limit junk‑food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund budget to hire 21,000 teachers; infant classes average 20, junior 25; extended school hours; 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Subject-specialist teaching in core subjects; reduce high‑stakes testing at 7 and 11; stronger SEN support; behaviour plans and managed transfers.
- Unified academic/vocational diplomas from 14; fund parity for colleges; maintain statutory school transport distances.
- Green building standards for education estates; strengthen outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders and equality
- 10,000 more police (funded by scrapping ID cards) plus complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy, modernise tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences; anti‑social behaviour tools with underlying support.
- Prisons focused on work, literacy and skills; progress tied to effort.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; tighten judicial control of any control orders; allow intercept evidence; repeal flawed terror provisions.
- Overhaul asylum processing via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; pursue EU common standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units in every force.

Economy and business
- Stamp Duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simpler, lighter regulation with impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small‑business rate relief and site‑value rating; fair‑trading duty; English Tourism Board.
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for cleaner vehicles and energy‑efficient homes.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no replacement of aging nuclear plants.

Pensions, benefits and family support
- From 75: basic state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; residency‑based “citizen’s pension.”
- Replace Council Tax to benefit most pensioners; six months’ maternity pay at minimum‑wage rate.
- Tailored employment support replacing one‑size‑fits‑all schemes; end harsh sanctions on genuine claimants.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC‑based assessment/enforcement plus specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working‑age people; option to invest a year’s payment in insulation.
- Strengthen protection for failed occupational pensions; consult and honour accrued public‑sector pension rights.
- Reduce fraud/error through simplification and prevention.

Housing, local services and environment
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; encourage brownfield reuse via VAT reform; require permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; increase core arts funding with inflation; support grassroots sport.
- Devolve more powers; streamline inspectorates; protect post offices and universal postal service.
- Zero‑waste goal; 60% household recycling within seven years; producer responsibility; climate‑aware planning/building rules.

Transport
- Rail reform with fewer, longer franchises; shift road funds to station safety and key upgrades.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty to zero for least‑polluting cars; expand congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty and VED.
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for pensioners, disabled people, families and youth.
- Limit major new roads; grow rail freight; develop ports/waterways; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new SE expansions.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Fair‑trading duty and Food Trade Inspector to protect farm gate prices.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act with conservation zones and regional co‑management; stronger wildlife protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act.
- Precaution on GM crops, support GM‑free zones, rigorous labelling; promote organic.

Europe, international affairs and defence
- Support EU institutional reform subject to referendum; prepare for euro entry if conditions met.
- Iraq: back democratic transition, build Iraqi capacity, and aim to withdraw forces with UN mandate expiry.
- Multilateral security, UN and EU reform, human rights focus.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reprioritise programmes; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms‑export oversight; back an international arms trade treaty.
- International development: increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; fair trade access; responsible investment; green development priorities; stronger action on global environmental crime; lead on climate targets (Kyoto plus “contraction and convergence”).

Constitution and governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; reduce departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; fair funding across the UK.
- Extend STV to local and national elections; predominantly elected second chamber; voting age aligned with other civic responsibilities; reform BBC governance via an independent regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; merge key portfolios into a single environment/transport/energy department.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals and commitments

- Economy and tax: Maintain a 2% inflation target and fiscal rules; keep net debt prudent. No rise in basic or top income tax and no VAT on essentials; targeted support for families. Deliver £21bn efficiency savings. Raise the minimum wage to £5.05 (Oct 2005) and £5.35 (Oct 2006). Aim for an 80% employment rate via welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform (Pathways to Work). Support enterprise, manufacturing and procurement; keep competitive corporation tax and R&D credits. Ten‑year science strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014. Energy policy to balance climate and security with renewables, nuclear, clean coal and microgeneration.

- Transport: Invest over £180bn to 2015; improve rail reliability, consider new high‑speed lines and fund Crossrail; upgrade London Underground. Expand key motorways, manage congestion and consider national road pricing. Free off‑peak local bus travel for over‑60s and disabled people; stronger local powers over buses; promote cycling, walking and road safety. Press to include aviation in EU emissions trading; expand UK shipping under tonnage tax.

- Education and skills: Personalised learning; multiyear school funding with a guaranteed per‑pupil uplift. All secondary schools to be specialist and extended; target at least 200 Academies by 2010; nationwide rebuilding of secondary schools (BSF) and a 15‑year primary upgrade. Stronger discipline and support for special educational needs. 14–19 reforms with specialised diplomas; more apprenticeships and reformed FE. In HE, fees capped at £3,000 with grants and bursaries; expand participation toward 50% and increase PhD support.

- NHS and public health: Investment tripling by 2008; maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008; free choice of hospital. Expand primary and community services, including modern community hospitals; use independent/voluntary capacity at NHS standards. Tougher action on MRSA and streamlined management. More NHS dentists; better patient information. Improve school meals and nutrition standards; clearer food labelling; curb junk food advertising to children. Restrict smoking in most enclosed workplaces and public places; expand cessation services and health trainers; universal access to school nurses.

- Crime, justice and security: Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide; expand Community Support Officers and a single non‑emergency number. Wider powers against antisocial behaviour and alcohol‑related disorder. Drug testing on arrest with compulsory assessment; establish the Serious Organised Crime Agency; restructure for regional/national threats. Violent Crime Reduction Bill (replica guns, knives, air guns); tougher sentences and comprehensive offender management with post‑release supervision and tagging. Stronger asset recovery; corporate manslaughter law. Borders: introduce a points‑based migration system, English for settlement, employer penalties, biometric visas, e‑borders and phased ID cards; faster asylum decisions. Counter‑terror measures including control orders and new offences.

- Families and older people: Halve child poverty by 2010–11 through tax credits, childcare and employment; expand Sure Start Children’s Centres to 3,500 by 2010; free nursery education to 15 hours/week (towards 20); extended schools 8am–6pm; broader childcare support. Increase paid maternity leave to 9 months in 2007 (aim for 12) and extend flexible working (consultations for carers/older children). For older people: Pension Credit maintained; free off‑peak bus travel; consult on long‑term pensions reform; end unjustified compulsory retirement before 65; right to request work after 65; individual care budgets and better support for carers.

- Housing and communities: Expand home ownership; raise the stamp duty threshold; focus new supply in growth areas and regeneration where demand is weak; widen shared ownership. Ensure all social housing is decent by 2010; increase new social homes by 50% by 2008; enable councils to build; expand choice‑based lettings. Rural support for post offices, buses, affordable homes; CAP/CFP reform; environmental stewardship; Animal Welfare Bill.

- Fairness at work and equality: Deliver a package including at least four weeks’ paid holiday in addition to bank holidays; enforce protections against discrimination (age, religion/belief, sexual orientation, gender, disability); narrow the gender pay gap; strengthen disability rights with personalised support. Create a Commission on Equality and Human Rights and a Single Equality Act.

- International, defence, development and climate: Active role in the EU (referendum on the Constitutional Treaty), with NATO as defence cornerstone; euro decision based on five economic tests. Counter WMD proliferation; support stability in Iraq and Afghanistan; pursue Middle East peace. Retain the independent nuclear deterrent; modernise armed forces; prioritise veterans. Development: reach 0.7% of national income for aid by 2013; debt relief; anti‑corruption; International Finance Facility; aim for universal AIDS treatment by 2010 and free basic health and education in poor countries. Climate: meet Kyoto; target −20% CO2 by 2010 and −60% by 2050; expand renewables, efficiency and emissions trading.

- Culture, sport, media, digital and environment: Free entry to national museums; renew regional museums; expand cultural access in schools; invest in grassroots sport and facilities; guarantee 2 hours PE plus 2–3 extra hours weekly by 2010; support the 2012 Olympics legacy. Reform BBC governance via a new Trust; guarantee the licence fee for the Charter; complete digital switchover 2008–2012; modernise IP and introduce film tax relief. Strengthen local environmental powers; universal kerbside recycling of at least two materials by 2010; focus new homes on brownfield; protect/enhance green belt; Marine Act; apply a sustainable building code for publicly funded homes from 2006.

- Democracy, devolution and local government: Complete House of Lords reform (remove remaining hereditaries, codify conventions, limit bill time; free vote on composition). Devolve further powers to Wales, London and regions; work to restore Northern Ireland institutions contingent on ending paramilitarism. Empower neighbourhoods with budgets, by‑laws and service triggers; extend parish councils to London. Support social enterprises in public services. Create a national youth volunteering framework. Give councils more freedoms, three‑year funding and fewer inspections; consider more elected mayors and whole‑council elections. Cap excessive council tax rises and improve take‑up of council tax benefit.
